LESSON: DESCANT RECORDER

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS AND SPORTS
Strand: Creating and Performing
Topic 2.7: Descant Recorder

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Descant Recorder. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: What is the importance of applying technique when playing instrumental music?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify the fingering of notes in the scale of F major
2. perform a solo piece in F major on a descant recorder, applying correct playing techniques
3. value playing music on the descant recorder
4. describe the format of a play script
5. create a one act play addressing a societal issue
6. recognise play performance as a channel of addressing societal issues

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: DESCANT RECORDER
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS AND SPORTS · Grade: Grade 9
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Descant Recorder helps you succeed in CREATIVE ARTS AND SPORTS. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: DESCANT RECORDER
Study Descant Recorder like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Identify the fingering of notes in the scale of F major

What this means
In this part you learn to identify the fingering of notes in the scale of F major. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify the fingering of notes in the scale of F major.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Descant Recorder” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify the fingering of notes in the scale of F major. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Descant Recorder is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Descant Recorder” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: identify the fingering of notes in the scale of F major)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Descant Recorder in your own words. (skill: perform a solo piece in F major on a descant recorder, applying correct playing techniques)

Example 3: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson. (skill: value playing music on the descant recorder)

Example 4: Show how “Descant Recorder” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: describe the format of a play script)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Descant Recorder to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify the fingering of notes in the scale of F major.
3. Practise this skill: perform a solo piece in F major on a descant recorder, applying correct playing techniques.
4. Practise this skill: value playing music on the descant recorder.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Descant Recorder from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Descant Recorder: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 9 learner study Descant Recorder?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. What is the importance of applying technique when playing instrumental music?
2. How can a play performance be made believable to an audience?
3. Why is it important to decorate props to be used for performance?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Descant Recorder means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify the fingering of notes in the scale of F major.
5. Be able to: perform a solo piece in F major on a descant recorder, applying correct playing techniques.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.
